1. Claimants being major children of Smt. Kamlesh have
approached Claims Tribunal, South West Dwarka seeking
compensation for death of their mother in motor vehicle accident
being subject matter of Fir No.216/15 under section
279/337/304A Ipc, Ps Sector-23, Dwarka, New Delhi.
Background

2. Brief facts culled from application read with Final Report would reveal that Smt. Kamlesh riding the pillion of Scooty No.HR-26BA-0627 driven by her son Ashwani Kumar met with an accident near Bharat Petroleum, Bijwasan, Dwarka Underpass, New Delhi on 17.06.2015 at around 9:00 AM after Oil Tanker No. HR-58A-7804 driven at high speed in rash and negligent manner hit their scooty from behind as a result of which Smt. Kamlesh fell down on the road and got crushed under the wheels of the Tanker.
She was immediately taken to DDU Hospital, New Delhi where injured was declared ' Brought Dead'.

3. It is submitted that accident resulting in death of Smt.
Kamlesh took place due to rash and negligent driving of Oil Tanker No.HR-58A-7804 by Lokesh Kumar (driver) which vehicle was registered in the name of Prabhmannat Singh MACT No. 192/2016 Raj Kumar Vs.

 Chaman Lal sustained fatal injuries in a  motor vehicle accident dt. 17.06.2015  caused due to rash or negligent driving of  vehicle (Tanker) No. HR-58A-7804 being  driven by Respondent No.1 owned by  Respondent No.2 and Insured by R3/The MACT No. 192/2016 Raj Kumar Vs. HR-58A-7804 after their scooty was hit from behind by the Tanker near Bharat Petroleum, Bijwasan on 17.06.2015.
15. His testimony remained consistent and suggestion imputing negligence of the deponent (PW-1) has been denied during cross-examination of witness by ld. counsel for insurance company.

16. Respondent Lokesh Kumar (driver) despite being indicted of rash and negligent driving of the Tanker resulting in death of Smt. Kamlesh due to injury sustained in motor vehicle accident has not entered witness-box to rebut the allegation and adverse inference is required to be raised against the driver as per the dicta of Hon'ble High Court of Orissa in National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Durdadshya Kumar Samal & Ors. 1987 SCC Online Ori. 57 AND Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Vs. Smt. Kamlesh & Ors. decided by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi on 11th November, 2008.

Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530.

. The standard  of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not  have been applied...."

19. Similar observation has been recorded by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
